result:
For $k\ge d$, every pure $d$-dimensional complex is $k$-decomposable. Any facet $\sigma$ has $|\sigma|=d+1\le k+1$, and deleting it leaves a pure $d$-dimensional complex whose link is $\{\varnothing\}$, a simplex. Repeatedly deleting facets reaches a single facet, so the recursion always succeeds. Since every intermediate $\Delta_i$ is pure of dimension $d$, any ordering of the missing $(d+1)$-sets works, and no new vertices are needed. So $b(d,k)=0$ for $k\ge d$.

For $k<d$, I am recalling rather than deriving the bound. I believe the known extension result uses $d-k$ new vertices and that this is sharp, which gives $b(d,k)=d-k$ in that range. Combining the two cases gives $\max(0,\,d-k)$. I did not verify the lower bound or the sharpness for $k<d$.

ANSWER: $\max(0,\,d-k)$
